scope: Hardcoded identity, biography, availability, response-time, contact, positioning, capability, metric, testimonial, experience, education, course, social, resume, and legal claims rendered by public routes
Repository-defined Project and Article records, public fallbacks, metadata, and publication assumptions
Current five-pillar coverage in public source code
limitations: This is a source-code audit, not proof of a person's identity, employment, education, client relationship, account ownership, or consent.
No production database export, private worksheet, resume contents, certificates, contracts, analytics, or testimonial consent records were available or inspected.
Publicly rendered contact values are redacted here to avoid duplicating personal data; their source locations remain listed.
A repeated value in source code is not treated as independent real-world verification.

status_contract.verified-by-code: The statement is limited to deterministic behavior or configuration visible in this repository. It does not verify an external personal or commercial fact.
status_contract.needs-owner-verification: The source currently asserts a real-world fact. Production publication is blocked until the owner confirms it and records an evidence/consent reference outside Git.
status_contract.remove: The current value is contradictory, generic, unsafe as a factual fallback, unsupported social proof, simulated behavior, stale, or outside the approved positioning; it must not be published as truth.
status_contract.dynamic-derived: The value must be calculated from production-visible, truth-approved records using the stated derivation rule and must never be typed as a marketing number.

publication_contract.default_policy: Deny publication unless a field is explicitly approved and its content_tier, verification_state, status, and visibility all pass the production gate.
production: Use content_tier=production only; exclude demo and fixture records in repository/service queries, not only in the UI.
Require verification_state=approved for every personal, employment, education, credential, client, testimonial, project-outcome, account-ownership, availability, response-time, and resume claim.
Require status=published, is_deleted=false, and visibility=public; scheduled records must also be inside their publish window.
Allow dynamic metrics only from the same production-visible, approved record set and return no metric when the source set is incomplete.
A missing fact must omit the component or use neutral UI copy; it must never fall back to a person, role, date, category, outcome, or number.
Testimonials require approved wording, identity/relationship, source reference, and publication consent as separate gates.
demo: Use content_tier=demo with deterministic demo IDs and an explicit synthetic=true marker.
Demo mode must be enabled only outside production, carry a visible Demo label, and set noindex/nofollow.
Synthetic names, companies, testimonials, clients, outcomes, employment, and education must never be copied into production seeds.
Production APIs must reject attempts to publish demo or synthetic records.
private_evidence: Store evidence references, consent files, private contact details, client confidentiality notes, contracts, certificates, and resume source files outside Git with access control.

The committed manifest may store only an opaque evidence reference state such as pending or approved; it must not store evidence URLs, document IDs, phone numbers, addresses, or confidential client details.
Verification changes require verifier identity, timestamp, reason, and an audit event; revocation immediately removes the affected public claim.

dynamic_record_contracts.current_repository_state: A MongoDB Project model and UI exist, but there are no versioned production project records or seeds to audit. The current model lacks content_tier, verification_state, public visibility, project kind, primary pillar, evidence references, explicit owner role, outcome provenance, and per-resource confidentiality controls.
required_truth_fields: stable public slug and owner-approved title/summary/content
primary pillar plus optional secondary pillars
owner role, team context, structured start/end/release dates, and ongoing state
stack plus architecture, security, performance, accessibility, AI, and system-design decisions that are actually evidenced
outcomes with metric value, unit, baseline, measurement window, method, and evidence approval; otherwise qualitative only
client/collaborator identity visibility and confidentiality policy
live/source/resource URL visibility with ownership and disclosure approval
media provenance, alt text, and public File references
content_tier, verification_state, status, visibility, verifier audit metadata, and published revision
publication_rules: Only completed, non-deleted, production, approved, public records may appear publicly.
Client work defaults to anonymized identity and hidden source/live links until each disclosure is approved.
